WHISTLEBLOWERS 2022

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Carte Blanche explores the phenomenon of whistleblowers and why it’s more important than ever to protect these brave resistors who choose to challenge the faciliators - despite the risk to themselve

Unique Selling Point:
** NEWS - WE NEED TO STAY CURRENT
** WE GIVE CONTEXT TO STORIES THAT DOMINATE NEWS WITH A DIFFERENT ANGLE RATHER THAN STRAIGHT UP REPORTING ON EVENTS
** ONE OF JOY's STORIES IS MENTIONED IN THE ORIGINAL STATE CAPTURE REPORT - WE NEED TO OWN IT.

Summary:
Whistleblowers distrupt the course of corruption, but stepping up, comes with a target on their backs. Death threats, murder, a life in hiding – these are not movie plots, this is the reality for whitsleblowers in South Africa.

We speak to South Africans who walk the line in an attempt to expose fraud and corruption at the risk of their own lives. And explore what the country is doing to the protect them.

Further information:
What would you do if you had access to damning information that could take down corrupt individuals. Some have fled the country, others are in hiding and the unlucky ones... are dead. As the Zondo Commission on State Capture closes another chapter, we come face to face with the whistleblowers on the frontline in the fight against fraud and corruption.
If government can’t protect these people – why would anyone come forward?

INTERVIEWS
1. MANDY WEINER – EXPERT – LOTS OF EXPERIENCE DEALING WITH WHISTLEBLOWERS – WROTE THE BOOK, STILL DEALS WITH SOURCES REGULARLY - SHOOT IN 702 STUDIO
2. GIDEON POGRUND – GIBS – MOST RECENT STUDY ON WHISTLEBLOWING IN SA – TRIUMPHS & TRIBULATIONS - SHOOT AT GIB // OFFICE STYLE – WILL FIGURE SOMETHING OUT TO MAKE IT COOL
3. ATHOL WILLIAMS - ZOOM INTERVIEW – WILL SHOOT NICELY, LOTS OF CREATIVE ANGLES, IN DOORS MOODY
4. THEMBA MASEKO – AT HIS HOME – WHAT IT MEANS TO STAY AND FACE THE MUSIC
5. THABISO ZULU - AN ORIGINAL WHISTLEBLOWER – PRE-ZONDO – HE HAS BEEN SHOT AND IS CONSTANTLY IN HIDING. SHOOT WHATSAPP VIDEO CALL.

Babita Deokaran has been silenced, Thabiso has been gunned down but lives to tell the tale, while Athol has left the country in fear of his life, and Themba is facing the reality of what it means to speak out and stay put.

The idea is to touch on the dangers of being a whistleblower – but to humanise it with their personal stories – and how they cope with the aftermath and the fall out. We touch on their whistleblowing briefly, but explore their experience post speaking out. Our experts frame how crucial it is for South Africa that we protect these people and nurture a culture of whistleblowers – because at the moment the prospect of speaking out is not such an attractive one for those who may be watching from wings armed with more explosive evidence that could blow up corrupt cabals who continue lurk and loot.

TREATMENT
I’m thinking like an espionage / spy feel…. Not that whistleblowers are spies, but they reveal so-called secrets – so moody lighting, slider on second cam. And then some stylized shots around documents, money and sneaky calls… Will speak to Jan about some kind of graphic with some whistleblower images.










Extra Budget Items:
We’ll need to get some Zondo Commission Footage, some images of whistleblowers.

STRUCTURE

THEMBA: when the night comes, that's when we start worrying and making sure that all the doors are locked. // T2M9

VISUAL BREATHER 2 seconds – ek het ‘n shot van ‘n hand wat ‘n deur sluit

THABISO: They've tried to kill me, but I'm still I'm still alive// I'm waiting for my day to die.

VISUAL BREATHER 2 seconds

ATHOL: // I was not going to wait until there was a gun to my head.

LINK: Death threats, murder, a life in hiding – these are not movie plots, this is the reality for whistle-blowers in South Africa.

VO: Resisting coercion in the culture of corruption and speaking out against the blatant looting of state coffers, sadly, does not go unpunished in this country.

THEMBA: // I decided I was going to defy both Zuma and Ajay Gupta. And that eventually led to my exit from government.

VO: Former Government Communication and Information System CEO Themba Maseko was instructed to direct government’s R600 million advertising budget to The New Age, a Gupta owned newspaper. He refused.

THEMBA: I got a cold shoulder from my political establishment, my friends and comrades. People stopped answering calls. I stopped receiving calls.
VISUAL BEAT
VO: Ostracising whistleblowers takes the fight against corruption down a dangerous road. Mandy Wiener is a talkshow host and journalist.

MANDY: Whistleblowers cannot be treated as pariahs ,as impimpis. They cannot be pushed to the fringes of society. // If we don't have whistleblowers, it means that corruption will continue unabated, it means that our democracy will be eroded //

LINK: Speaking truth to power casts a spotlight on dodgy dealings usually hidden in the shadows at the expense of the country, the economy and its citizens. But those that lurk in the dark, don’t go without a fight.

VO: More than two years after his testimony at the Zondo Commission, the first volume of findings on state capture was released in January - and Maseko was reminded that there is a cost to raising the alarm.

THEMBA: Those were the worst 10 minutes of my life.

VO: An attempted home invasion left the Maseko’s terrified.

THEMBA: I was with my wife screaming. I was shouting, We're trying to get help, and these people were running up and down the roof.

VO: The intruders avoided CCTV cameras as they moved through the property.

THEMBA: // it was a bit dark, but I could see a human being right on top of a roof. And literally froze
MASA: And you're basically staring at him. He's staring at you.
THEMBA: // at that point, I'm screaming at the wife to say, please press the panic button. //
MASA: What was that like hearing your wife frantically screaming?
THEMBA: It was terrifying. I just said she must look herself in the bathroom and make sure she's safe.//

VO: Maseko is convinced it was not a random home invasion - he believes the intent was to send a message.

THEMBA: the fact that nothing was stolen when in fact it was possible to break any of the glasses in the house was clearly an indication that it was an attempt to intimidate me. //
LINK: When threats turn into actions, the consequences can be sobering. Last year, a key witness in a R332-million PPE scandal was gunned down outside her home in broad day light – Babita Deokaran was silenced for good.
VO: In December, Deokaran received a posthumous international special recognition award alongside a fellow whistleblower. This man is Thabiso Zulu – there’s been attempts to discredit him, he has been hunted down, beaten and shot - for speaking out on municipal corruption in KwaZulu Natal.
.
He spoke to us from an undisclosed location in rural KZN.

MASA: Hi Thabiso, your signal is not great – let’s try this – are you still in hiding?
THABISO: //I hate to use the term hiding. I prefer to say I move around. I sleep in different places. // I'm not a victim in this. I'm a participant in the struggle against corruption,

VO: Last year, Zulu’s enemies tracked him down to a location where he was staying with his 10 year old son.

THABISO: The fear in the eyes of my son saying, Baba, are they going to kill us? //I don't mind dying, but I don't want to die with my son, // He hasn't done anything in this world T1M8

VO: The attackers were interrupted and while both Zulu and his son were unharmed - the message hit home.

The stakes are high - and as the facilitators of fraud and corruption feel the net closing in, they even turn on those close to whistleblowers.

THABISO: My mother was threatened with rape by operatives of the state, // They threatened her with rape just because I'm a whistleblower. // /In the XHOSA CULTURE, there is something that is called omerta. You saw nothing. You heard nothing, you know, nothing. // If you speak it, you've broken an unwritten rule //

VO: But keeping quiet, is not an option, these crusaders of justice, could live with.

THABISO: I'm a warrior. My mother is a warrior. My grandmother is a warrior.// if there is a bullet out there with my name, it will find me one day, but it will find me wearing my own boots in the fight against corruption fighting. T2M7

VO: But the fight against corruption appears to have stagnated, according to the 2021 global Corruption Perceptions Index.

MANDY: Corruption in South Africa is endemic, and we are simply not doing enough to fight it. // we have to entice whistleblowers to come forward. We have to stack the cards in their favour, and the only way to do that is if they are sufficiently protected M1M4

VO: It’s a long way to go until the count ry gets to that point. Whistleblower Athol illiams fled South Africa in November last year.

ATHOL: //I never thought I'd be running for my life. // It's literally black and white. It's the opposite entirely of what I thought this experience would be. //A1M12

VO: Williams testified before the Zondo Commission alleging high-level corruption at SARS, implicating the US-based management consultancy firm he worked for as a senior partner.

There were rumblings of heightened risk around his safety months earlier, but the threat sunk in when Babita Deokaran was murdered in August 2021.

ATHOL: // it was a quick decision. // we lived in an apartment in Cape Town, and so we put that up for rent -//put// things in storage, literally just left with two bags with my with my passport, my credit card. That was it.
MASA: // That couldn’t have been an easy decision?
ATHOL: // it was almost a twilight zone for me, . // I've lived overseas, before I've studied overseas, before. So the act of leaving a home was familiar to me /In my head I felt dizzy and spinning because it just didn't make sense to me. And we were we were in tears. // It was that sense of I've done something wrong. If this is what I'm experiencing for having stood up and being a whistleblower//

MANDY: We have to change the way that whistleblowers are treated in South Africa, and that means changing how we think about them. So we need a change in the law, // // That would mean legal protection. It would mean psychological protection. It would mean ensuring that they have some kind of financial cushion. //we also need a societal revolution//

ATHOL: we stood up publicly, we’ve pointed to where the bad people are, we’ve named them, and then our society says, Well, now you're on your own. You were exposed. A1M17

VO: AFter testifying before the Zondo commission, Williams asked in vain to be afforded state protection.

MANDY: Our legislation doesn't cover whistleblowers in the way that it needs to. // All we have is the National Prosecuting Authorities Witness Protection Program. And that requires a whistleblower to actually be a witness in a criminal trial. //M1M3

LINK: Wheels of justice turn slowly, the facilitators carry on with their lives unaffected and those who broke rank bear the bunt of it

THEMBA: a lot of those people are living better lives than whistleblowers as we are sitting here // T2M14 // those who expose the corruption are sitting without jobs. They can't pay // their kids school fees. Some have lost their lives, and people's security is highly, highly at risk. And government is not blinking. //T2M15

VO: Trust in government has eroded, the economy has been crippled and the credibility of key institutions tainted. This is what state capture has brought about.

ATHOL: We are playing into the hands of the corrupt because no one's going to want to speak up// we will lose our fight against corruption and state capture. If we do not support and protect whistleblowers and no amount of talk by government or by corporations is going to change that. A1M19

MANDY: One of the recommendations from the Zondo Commission is around the remuneration of whistleblowers financially, and this is important because if you look at what happens in Europe and in the US, whistleblowers are eligible for between 10 and 50 per cent of a successful whistleblowing reward. M2M1

VO: It would go a long way to help whistleblowers in South Africa mitigate the backlash that comes with resisting corruption.

THEMBA: //my wife still is terrified. I'm equally terrified, T2M9 //I'm feeling unsafe in my own home, // did I do the right thing? Would I do it again? I think I would // try and understand more the security implications of financial implications. Kind of plan for those things in advance. But whether I would do it again, I don't have SHADOW OF A DOUBT that, I would do it again. T2M13
MASA: Any regrets?
ATHOL: // I can see the good it can do in our country. /// i think it comes at a cost unfortunately but i am proud to have served my country in this way and i absolutely would do it again.

VO: Giving up is simply not an option if it’s at the expense of South AFricans.

THABISO: // If I give up now, it's going to be a betrayal of those who have died in the struggle against corruption. // history will record that not every South African was silent. //We dodge bullets on daily basis. // Our own children will spit on our graves if we keep QUIET T1M2


PROMO 1 – 21 seconds
VO: Exposing grand corruption is honourable and courageous. But is it worth it?

THABISO: They've tried to kill me, but I'm still I'm still alive. // T1M14 I'm waiting for my day to die. T1M6

VO: Character Assassination. Intimidation. Death Threats. This is the life of a Whistleblower in South Africa.



PROMO 2 – 21 seconds
VO: Whistleblowers disrupt the course of corruption and in turn become targets.

THEMBA: the fact that nothing was stolen //was clearly an indication that it was an attempt to intimidate me. // T2M7

VO: We ask what’s the future of whistleblowing in South Africa, if those that speak out pay for it, often with their lives.


PROMO 3 – 11 seconds
VO: Stepping up as whistleblower is a deadly move – the threats are real. Some have fled the country, others are in hiding and the unlucky ones... are dead.

metadata.Summary: Whistleblowers distrupt the course of corruption, but stepping up, comes with a target on their backs. Death threats, murder, a life in hiding – these are not movie plots, this is the reality for whitsleblowers in South Africa. We speak to South Africans who walk the line in an attempt to expose fraud and corruption at the risk of their own lives. And explore what the country is doing to the protect them.
metadata.Further information: What would you do if you had access to damning information that could take down corrupt individuals. Some have fled the country, others are in hiding and the unlucky ones... are dead. As the Zondo Commission on State Capture closes another chapter, we come face to face with the whistleblowers on the frontline in the fight against fraud and corruption. If government can’t protect these people – why would anyone come forward? INTERVIEWS 1. MANDY WEINER – EXPERT – LOTS OF EXPERIENCE DEALING WITH WHISTLEBLOWERS – WROTE THE BOOK, STILL DEALS WITH SOURCES REGULARLY - SHOOT IN 702 STUDIO 2. GIDEON POGRUND – GIBS – MOST RECENT STUDY ON WHISTLEBLOWING IN SA – TRIUMPHS & TRIBULATIONS - SHOOT AT GIB // OFFICE STYLE – WILL FIGURE SOMETHING OUT TO MAKE IT COOL 3. ATHOL WILLIAMS - ZOOM INTERVIEW – WILL SHOOT NICELY, LOTS OF CREATIVE ANGLES, IN DOORS MOODY 4. THEMBA MASEKO – AT HIS HOME – WHAT IT MEANS TO STAY AND FACE THE MUSIC 5. THABISO ZULU - AN ORIGINAL WHISTLEBLOWER – PRE-ZONDO – HE HAS BEEN SHOT AND IS CONSTANTLY IN HIDING. SHOOT WHATSAPP VIDEO CALL. Babita Deokaran has been silenced, Thabiso has been gunned down but lives to tell the tale, while Athol has left the country in fear of his life, and Themba is facing the reality of what it means to speak out and stay put. The idea is to touch on the dangers of being a whistleblower – but to humanise it with their personal stories – and how they cope with the aftermath and the fall out. We touch on their whistleblowing briefly, but explore their experience post speaking out. Our experts frame how crucial it is for South Africa that we protect these people and nurture a culture of whistleblowers – because at the moment the prospect of speaking out is not such an attractive one for those who may be watching from wings armed with more explosive evidence that could blow up corrupt cabals who continue lurk and loot. TREATMENT I’m thinking like an espionage / spy feel…. Not that whistleblowers are spies, but they reveal so-called secrets – so moody lighting, slider on second cam. And then some stylized shots around documents, money and sneaky calls… Will speak to Jan about some kind of graphic with some whistleblower images.
